title: BrainWideBench: Benchmarking large-scale pretraining and across-animal transfer in multi-region neural recordings
why_read: A neuroscience benchmark for testing whether large-scale brain recordings from many mice can produce transferable representations, relevant mainly to computational neuroscience researchers.
analysis: BrainWideBench is a benchmark built on a large dataset of neural recordings from 139 mice across 276 brain regions doing a decision-making task, meant to test whether pretraining on this data yields representations that generalize across animals and tasks. It evaluates three things: predicting behavior from neural activity, predicting future or masked neural activity, and recovering known anatomical structure. The paper finds pretraining helps over single-session baselines but that no single method does well on all three evaluation types, showing this is still an open problem. This is a niche but well-constructed benchmark paper for the computational neuroscience community, less directly relevant to typical software engineers but interesting to those working on foundation models for biological data.
